proposals.name: Civic Order Patrolmaton
proposals.entry:
Official Designation: Civic Order Patrolmaton
Abbreviation: C.O.P.
Common Name: Patrolmaton
Street Names: Tinner, Tinners, Cop, Cops
Affiliation: Civic Vigilance
Role: Patrol, arrest, riot suppression, checkpoint enforcement
Origin: Imported from one of the Hundred Kingdoms
Operational Command: Skyport Station
Scale: 1

The Civic Order Patrolmaton, or C.O.P., is the mechanical constable of modern Fogport.

They are impossible to mistake for human officers.

A Patrolmaton stands considerably taller than an ordinary Fogporter, its proportions exaggerated by exceptionally long arms and legs. Beneath its cheap stamped-metal uniform are exposed iron mechanisms, wooden structural members, cables, springs and heavy mechanical joints. Its helmet is a crude metal reproduction of the traditional Civic Vigilance constable's helmet.

Two illuminated eyes burn from an otherwise expressionless mechanical face.

Fogporters call them Tinners. Or, increasingly, simply Cops.

Fifteen Years of Cops

Patrolmatons began appearing on Fogport streets approximately fifteen years ago following a serious internal crisis within Civic Vigilance.

The Civic Order publicly described their introduction as an economy measure. Tinners required no wages, pensions, meals or sleeping quarters and could remain on duty for extraordinary periods.

The machines proved particularly useful for work that human officers disliked: riot lines, dangerous arrests, night patrols and prolonged checkpoints.

Their numbers have increased steadily ever since.

Human Vigilance officers remain common, particularly as investigators, supervisors and administrators. But when the Civic Order expects violence, it increasingly sends Tinners.

A Policeman's Mind

A Patrolmaton is not mindless. Within its intended field it possesses roughly average human intelligence.

A Tinner can recognize crimes, question witnesses, pursue suspects, establish a perimeter, search a building, control a crowd, coordinate with other officers and make tactical decisions without waiting for instructions.

It can also arrest someone entirely on its own authority.

A human Vigilance officer does not need to be standing nearby for a Tinner's command to be legally binding under Civic Order law.

Outside its professional knowledge, however, a Patrolmaton's intelligence becomes considerably less impressive.

Ask one whether a man broke a window and it can conduct an investigation. Ask one whether breaking the window was morally justified and you may be there awhile.

The Skyport Signal

Patrolmatons maintain radio contact with the Civic Vigilance command station in the restricted Crown of Skyport Station.

Tall aerials and transmission equipment at Skyport send coded instructions across Fogport. Orders can redirect patrols, establish cordons, identify wanted persons or summon nearby Tinners to an emergency.

This allows something human policing never permitted: dozens of officers receiving the same order almost simultaneously.

During major disturbances, Tinners can also be dispatched from Skyport aboard the small red Civic Vigilance zeppelins bearing the eye insignia.

Seeing one overhead is unpleasant. Seeing it stop above your street is worse.

Maintenance

Patrolmatons are maintained by the Civic Order Guild of Mechanical Servitors, Automata & Municipal Engines, usually shortened to the Servitor Guild.

Guild mechanics operate workshops throughout Fogport, with their largest Patrolmaton facility beneath Skyport.

A damaged Tinner is not considered injured. It is “out of service.”

A destroyed one is “beyond economical repair.”

This terminology occasionally causes arguments when a Tinner is lying in several pieces in somebody's parlor.

Typical Civic Order Patrolmaton — Fate

Scale 1

Patrolmatons receive the normal Scale advantage against ordinary Scale 0 people when their superior physical size, strength, durability or reach matters. They should feel genuinely dangerous rather than simply having inflated skill numbers.

Aspects

High Concept: Civic Order Patrolmaton
Trouble: A Policeman's Mind in a Complicated World
Aspect: Long Arms of the Law
Aspect: Orders From Skyport
Aspect: Built to Stand Where Men Would Run

Skills

Great (+4): Physique
Good (+3): Fight, Notice
Fair (+2): Athletics, Shoot, Provoke
Average (+1): Investigate, Will, Drive, Crafts

Their Crafts represents practical knowledge of their own mechanisms and other Patrolmatons, not general mechanical expertise.

Stress

Physical: 4 boxes
Mental: 2 boxes
Consequences: Standard

Stunts

Crowd Suppression: +2 to Provoke when ordering a crowd to disperse, surrender, clear a street or submit to Civic authority.

Long Reach: The Patrolmaton's elongated arms allow it to Fight across obstacles or reach people who would ordinarily be outside immediate melee range.

Mechanical Constable: +2 to Notice or Investigate when identifying behavior associated with a crime, locating a fleeing suspect or detecting someone attempting to evade a police cordon.

Never Tires: A Patrolmaton does not suffer ordinary exhaustion from marching, standing watch, pursuing someone or remaining at its post.

Typical Equipment

Heavy truncheon, Civic Vigilance pistol, mechanical restraints, signal receiver, whistle, lantern and occasionally a heavy patrol blade.

A single Tinner should be a serious problem for Byl and Lott. Two should change their plans.

A line of six advancing shoulder-to-shoulder should be treated less like six ordinary NPCs and more like a moving piece of street architecture that wants to arrest you.

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
They Don't Receive Orders the Way Everyone Thinks

The Skyport broadcasts don't directly control the Patrolmatons. They transmit instructions.

A Tinner interprets those instructions and decides how to execute them.

The Civic Order has been extremely careful not to publicize this distinction.

There is therefore no master switch at Skyport that turns every Cop into a puppet—and no guarantee that every Cop will interpret an unusual order identically.

The Servitor Guild Has Learned Something

The Civic Order does not possess the complete specifications for the Patrolmatons. It never did.

The foreign manufacturer supplied maintenance manuals, replacement schedules and approved procedures, but several sealed mechanisms inside every Patrolmaton were explicitly designated “manufacturer service only.”

Fogport is at war-adjacent distance from the manufacturer now. Replacement parts became difficult to obtain. So the Servitor Guild eventually opened one.

Inside the cranial mechanism they discovered something nobody expected: there is considerably more machinery devoted to memory than policing requires.

The Guild quietly closed it again. Only a handful of senior mechanics know.

Old Cops Remember

Patrolmatons are routinely serviced, repaired and reassigned. Their operational records are supposedly cleared during major overhauls.

They aren't.

Some of the oldest Tinners operating in Fogport contain fragments of fifteen years of patrol experience: faces, addresses, arrests, conversations and orders.

And, potentially, what actually happened during the Civic Vigilance crisis that caused the government to purchase them in the first place.

A Tinner standing motionless at an intersection may recognize someone it arrested twelve years ago. It simply has no reason to mention it.

The Forbidden Order

Servitor Guild mechanics have identified an instruction buried deep within the machines' original command architecture.

They cannot determine what it does. It isn't written in Fogport's command vocabulary. It came from the kingdom that manufactured them.

The Civic Order has never transmitted it. As far as anyone knows.

Adventure Hooks

The Cop Who Won't Arrest Him: A wanted man walks directly past a Patrolmaton. The machine recognizes him, checks the warrant and deliberately allows him to leave.

Dead Air: Skyport's Civic Vigilance transmitter stops broadcasting for eleven minutes. Across Fogport, every Tinner independently decides what its standing orders require.

Officer 19: An ancient, heavily repaired Patrolmaton approaches Byl and quietly asks him a question: “Do you remember me?” Byl has never seen it before.

Manufacturer's Representative: A foreign airship docks at Skyport. Its passenger carries credentials from the company that originally manufactured Fogport's Patrolmatons—and requests access to every unit in the city.

The Wrong Signal: Every Tinner within three blocks abruptly stops what it is doing, turns toward the same distant point in Fogport, and begins walking.

Nobody at Skyport sent the order.
